tip: Ter plus a participle, tenho corrido, means an action repeated up to now, not one finished event like English present perfect.
A gente means we but takes a singular verb, so it is a gente tem se comunicado, never têm.
Como se, meaning as if, takes the imperfect subjunctive, giving soubesse rather than the indicative sabia.
For a hypothetical, se plus the imperfect subjunctive tivesse pairs with the conditional ensinaria.
Quem dera expresses a wish, if only, and is followed by the imperfect subjunctive pudesse.
An impersonal opinion like era importante que forces the subjunctive, so soubessem, not sabiam.
Here quem means whoever or those who, and it takes a singular verb, so estuda and passa.
Tudo que is a set relative phrase for everything that; Brazilians usually drop the o of tudo o que.
Gostar always needs de before its object, so it is gosto de pessoas, never gosto pessoas.
For where a place is located, ficar is the natural verb, so a escola fica no centro means it sits downtown.
The object pronoun o here means him and sits before the verb, o contratou, meaning hired him.
Cobrir has the irregular participle coberto, not cobrido, as in tinha coberto o bolo.
Pagar has two participles; with ter use pagado, as in tínhamos pagado, while pago goes with ser or estar.
Procurar means look for and takes a direct object, so procurado emprego, with no preposition after it.
After a preposition, Portuguese often uses o qual, so trabalhar em gives o projeto no qual estamos trabalhando.
For a point in time a relative clause uses em que, not quando, so o dia em que nos conhecemos.
Todo mundo means everyone but takes a singular verb, as in todo mundo sabe, never todo mundo sabem.
Assistir meaning to watch formally takes a before its object, but Brazilians drop it, as in a série que estou assistindo.
